en: The Mātṛkābhedatantra, Chapter One.
On the delightful peak of Kailāsa, adorned with various jewels,
she questioned Bhairava, the Supreme Lord, with supreme devotion.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"O Lord, the worship of Tripurā is especially performed with gold and jewels;
likewise, in the Kali age, it is performed with gold, silver, and secret gems.
O Lord of Gods, by what means is gold, silver, and so forth obtained?"
Therefore, explain that in detail, so that there may be [knowledge of] gems and the like;
O treasure-house of compassion, tell that which has not been stated in any of the tantras.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain how gems and such are produced:
by means of my own fiery energy and mercury, what gem indeed cannot be obtained?
Likewise, even with common sea salt that is very white.
Listen attentively, O Goddess, to the varieties of *sambala*.
One should worship Siddhakālikā according to the Cīna-tantra;
or else, one should worship the supreme Goddess Dakṣiṇakālikā.
One should perform recitation and worship for seven days according to the procedure taught in the Kālītantra.
In the Satya age, it is one [unit]; in the Tretā, double; in the Dvāpara, threefold;
thus one should know that in the Kali age, the recitation is fourfold.
Having brought two *tulās* of provisions with great effort,
one should recite eight hundred times over the provisions the three seed-syllables— *vasu* (va), *ādya* (a), and *śiva* (śa)— adorned with *māyā* (ī) and the *bindu*. MBhT 1.9.
Having carefully brought milk produced from a black cow weighing eighty *tolakas*, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
then, one should cast a thread provided with cloth into the midst of the milk.
The wise one should produce heat by means of a very gentle fire.
When the drop has reached the limit of the Vedānta and is half-dried,
then one should lift that substance and cast it into the midst of water.
Then an examination must be performed; one should place [the substance] upon fire.
Having carefully lifted the smokeless substance from the vessel, one should recite the mantra consisting of the nine syllables that are worshipped by all right there.
Having brought pure and beautiful copper with great effort,
one should place one and a half *tolakas* of that copper into the midst of the fire.
Having observed that the copper has become like fire itself, one should carefully lift it up.
If one should apply that substance, the size of a *guñjā* seed, at that very moment,
it will certainly become silver— truly, truly so, O Girijā!
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
In what form is the cause that has the nature of milk, and in what form is Śaṅkara?
O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, please tell me that manner out of compassion.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
The wise one should bring a ṭaṅkana weighing four tolakas;
O Girijā, by means of the application of fire, he reduced it to the form of parched grain (lāja).
Then, having ground that with twice as much mango blossom, he should perform the mixing.

O Caṇḍikā, one should indeed recite the mantra of Mahāmāyā over it. O Daughter of the Mountain, if one makes this into a pill and causes a meeting [of substances], it will immediately take the form of milk; this is the truth, the absolute truth.
The illustrious Caṇḍikā said: "O Śaṅkara, by what means can liquor become devoid of scent?
I wish to hear all of that, if you have affection for me."
Śrī Śaṅkara said: Having taken the fragrance, one should write the auspicious [syllable] mounted upon fire (Ra), adorned with the left eye (Ū), and joined with the Bindu and Nāda. MBhT 1.22.

If the best of practitioners, having uttered the syllable *uhyatām*, should recite it one hundred and eight times, there will be the destruction of foul odors and other such things. *Mātṛkābhedatantra* 1.23.
The second chapter.
The venerable Goddess said:
"Speak, O Īśāna, O omniscient one, best among those who know all principles."
"O Lord, as for what you have said regarding my dwelling in union:
how is a son born, where does the semen reside,
how does the penis always increase in size, and how does its re-entry occur?"
"O Lord, I am indeed filled with fear; protect me from this peril of suffering! Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"The great lotus of Maṇipūra is situated in the center of the Suṣumṇā."

O Goddess of gods, its beautiful navel-lotus has a stalk; it is endowed with three curves and is always adorned with semen. Its stalk extends upward to the thousand-spoked [lotus], and thus it is adorned with semen.
Therefore, O Śivā, who consists of eternal bliss, that pair of breasts, which increases day by day,
has its stalk at the middle, ending within the Suṣumṇā; it is shaped like an eggplant (vṛntāka), very cool,
with the tip of the womb as its lower stalk.

Listen, O fortunate one of beautiful limbs: among those, the form that arises from the striking of the *liṅga* is supreme bliss; it does not exist anywhere in the three worlds. Listen with a concentrated mind to the nature of the navel-lotus.
The station of the *bindu* is in the center, eternally adorned with a lotus;
outside that, it has eight petals,
and further outside is a square [mandala] endowed with four gates, golden in luster and circular.
With its petals, there shall be a flower with a stalk consisting of three petals;
when the three petals have blossomed, blood is seen on the outer edge.
O Great Goddess, if within this there should be the striking of a *liṅga*, [the result follows].

When the semen has entered the center of the lotus, offspring are produced by that means. But when the semen of the man exceeds the blood of the woman, then, O Goddess, a daughter is born; if it is the reverse, a male is born.
If the semen of both is equal, a eunuch is certainly born.
Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs and good fortune, to the supreme greatness of the flower:
when it is joined with that semen in the middle, it increases day by day.
Thus, when the [proper] direction and month have arrived, that flower, together with its stalk, falls away, O Supreme Goddess; then the lineage becomes manifest. The Śrī Devī said:
When some disease arises, or when worms, insects, and the like appear, the life-force perishes from that; how then can that woman live? Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Priyaṃvadā, how can I describe the majesty of this flower? Within the center of the flower is the thousand-petaled abode of the Bindu;
where the bubbles abide, there indeed the lineage shall exist.
In this manner, O Goddess of the gods, if the lineage increases by a thousand in succession,
the great flower will flourish and no suffering whatsoever shall arise. O Great Sovereign, strive diligently to enjoy amorous play with me.
He who is the son in the monastery is celebrated as Gaṇeśa.
O Supreme Goddess, by the grace of your son,
creation is born upon the earth according to what is appropriate, free from obstacles.
Having heard this, O Goddess, the goddess, overwhelmed by the fire of passion,
was then embraced by Śiva in the form of Śivā. *Mātṛkābhedatantra* 2.22.
The third chapter.
The venerable Goddess said:
"O Lord, I have heard everywhere about enjoyment which provides nourishment for the senses."
"O bearer of Yoga, how do you say that one attains liberation through enjoyment?
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
Through enjoyment one attains Yoga; through enjoyment one achieves the means of the Kula."
Through enjoyment one attains perfection; through enjoyment one may attain liberation.
Therefore, enjoyment should always be practiced, along with external worship as desired.
O Priyamvadā, listen now to the rule for eating.
The power that resides in the *ādhāra*, having the form of a coiled serpent—O Supreme Goddess, the Self always abides in its center.
From that arises the desire for food; therefore, the one known as the *jīva* remains untainted.
She herself, though composed of qualities (guṇa), is directly called the "quality-less" (nirguṇa) individual soul (jīva).
O Goddess, the nourishment of the jīva is nothing but delusion; there is no doubt about this.
Kuṇḍalinī, endowed with the qualities, takes the form of the moon, the sun, and fire.
The wise practitioner should visualize that goddess extending from the *mūlādhāra* to the tip of the tongue;
having purified the fish, meat, and other offerings, he should place them before him, reciting the root mantra: "I offer [this] into the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī."
O Goddess, one should take each morsel while reciting this mantra. O Supreme Lady, the wise man should act in this manner with every morsel;
at that very moment he becomes the embodiment of Brahman—this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Mistress of the Gods.
For he who is intent on the thought, "The goddess Kuṇḍalinī is being enjoyed," shall attain success in mantra and success in knowledge, and not otherwise.
When this has been done, Hari himself becomes the form of Brahman and the form of Śiva.

Yoga-perfection shall be his, and the eight siddhis will come to pass. O Goddess, even that artificial and dreadful poison which is administered by enemies, upon consuming it, becomes nectar in that very instant; of this there is no doubt.
Substance purified by mantra becomes nectar through consumption.
O Dear One, when Kālakūṭa arose during the churning of the ocean,
I immediately consumed it at that very moment with this mantra.

"The goddess Kuṇḍalinī, who is of the form of a serpent and the supreme digit (kalā), is consumed in the form of a snake; therein lies a terrible poison. Thus, O beloved, has the procedure for the meal been told to you.
"O Maheśānī, all of this must be guarded in the midst of the multitude of bound souls (paśus).
The Śrī Devī said:
"Listen, O Lord, Supreme Bliss, whose nature consists of both the supreme and the non-supreme Kula."
"Tell me, O Supreme Lord, what is the sacrificial pit (homakuṇḍa) like?
Śrī Śiva said:
"Outside the Maṇipūra [cakra], there is the beautiful lotus of the navel."
Likewise, it may have eight petals or be circular; in its center, the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) is difficult to obtain.
O Goddess, that pit, which may be square or otherwise, takes on the form desired.
O Mistress of the Gods, a Brahmin is ordained as the performer for every kind of sacrificial pit.
O Goddess of the gods, the sacrificial pit (homakuṇḍa) for one born of the arms (the Kṣatriya) is circular, and that of the Vaiśya is a half-moon;
for one born of the feet (the Śūdra), it is triangular.
O Maheśānī, such is the pit, adorned with three stalks.
O beautiful Śivā, [the channel] with its upper stalk is adorned with supreme nectar in the thousand-petaled lotus; the middle stalk is in the navel-lotus and the root-support (mūlādhāra);
and the lower stalk, O Śivā, is at the tip of the embrace, consisting of eternal bliss.
O Goddess, this sacrificial fire-pit (homakuṇḍa) is prescribed in all tantras;
by the grace of the oblation performed therein, one becomes directly composed of Brahman.
Furthermore, for a Brahmin, the oblation of the *āhuti* is to be understood as fourfold.
O Goddess, for a Kṣatriya there are three [oblations], and for a Vaiśya two oblations;
for a Śūdra, O Goddess, there is one oblation, and liberation is likewise fourfold.
For a Brāhmaṇa it is Great Liberation (mahāmokṣa), and for a Kṣatriya it is union (sāyujya).
For one born of the Kṣatriya caste, there is residence in the same world (sārūpya); for those of the Śūdra caste, there is residence in the same realm (sālokya).
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) is indeed external for an external oblation;
therefore, the best of practitioners should fashion different types of pits according to the distinction of castes.
"In an external homa, the accomplishment of desired objects will occur; there is no doubt.
In the homa of knowledge, one attains the accomplishment of liberation; there is no doubt in this matter.
Thus, O beloved, I have told you the supreme essence of the tantras.
"One should not utter a curse against you, my beloved, in the presence of a beast.
The Goddess said:
"I have heard in all the Tantras that there is great merit in drinking wine."
"The distinction between the castes has not been told; reveal it now.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"O Pārvatī, there is no doubt that the Brahmin is the lord of all sacrifices."
In the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice and in the family tradition, there are four [classes], beginning with the Brāhmaṇas.
O Priyaṃvadā, for a Brāhmaṇa, there is great liberation even in the drinking of wine.
O Supreme Goddess, if a Brāhmaṇa should engage in drinking and so forth, [he attains that state].
At that very moment, O Daughter of the Mountain, he truly became Śiva in form— truly, truly so!
Just as water dissolves into water, as fire into fire,
as space when a jar is broken, and as wind into wind, O Beloved.

In the same way, O beloved Brahmā, by drinking wine a Brāhmaṇa merges into the Supreme Self, O Daughter of the Mountain; there is no doubt in this matter. Union and other forms of great liberation are ordained for Kṣatriyas and the other castes.
O Goddess, that woman is undoubtedly human in her drinking of wine.
Just as fire exists within the body in the form of a subtle thread, so too does Śivā;
the Great Thread is the form of austerity, and Hari is the form of worship.
O Goddess, wherever the great hook (*mahāṅkuśa*) increases and becomes joined,
that knowledge is certainly not obtained without the drinking of wine;
for this very reason, a Brahmin should always practice the drinking of wine.
"O Daughter of the Mountain, a Brāhmaṇa is not such merely by the recitation of the Mother of the Vedas;
O Goddess, when one possesses the knowledge of Brahman, only then is he called a Brāhmaṇa.
Brahman is the nectar of the gods, and this worldly liquor is its counterpart."
Because it possesses the nature of a spirit (*suratva*) through mere enjoyment, it is proclaimed as *surā*.
The three mantras should always be recited for liberation from the curse of Brahmā and other afflictions;
indeed, when performed by a twice-born (*dvija*), that *surā* becomes composed of Brahman (*brahmamayī*).
Just as fire becomes blazing by the mere placing of the oblation,
so too does wine bestow liberation by the mere act of releasing the curse.
For this very reason, O Goddess of gods, a Brahmin may consume the drink.
He is a Brahmin, he is a knower of the Vedas, he is an Agnihotrin, and he is one who has been initiated.
O Goddess, what need is there for much speaking? He alone is the essence of the three qualities (triguṇātmaka).
O Goddess, this path to liberation must be guarded against the multitude of bound souls (paśu).
Through disclosure, there would be loss of the body; otherwise, one is not to be censured. (MBhT 3.45, Chapter Four of the Mātṛkābhedatantra)
The illustrious Caṇḍikā said: "O Lord of the Gods, I have heard from your mouth in the Vedas and Purāṇas that great liberation is attained through the *nirmālya* of Śiva."
"Your offering remains are ungraspable; the cause, O All-pervading One, is ungraspable.
O Mahādeva, bearer of yoga, why do you speak words that are false? For, O Goddess, without a cause, there can be no such thing as the knowledge of liberation and so forth."
O Goddess, without the great conch (mahāśaṅkha), the mantra does not bestow success.
Furthermore, the garland consisting of Brahman itself is known by the name of the great conch;
it is [to be used] at the stone-press in Vṛndāvana, at the Gaṅgā, and in other places worshipped by the gods.
One must not touch the great conch at all; by touching it, one becomes like wood.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"The Gaṅgā is water, but liquor is the supreme cause."
"For indeed, garlands become pure by the mere touch of the causal [water].
O Lord of Gods, how is it that a garland becomes like a piece of wood by the touch of the Gaṅgā?
Tell me, O Supreme Lord; this is the doubt in my heart. (MBhT 4.5–6)

Śrī Śaṅkara said: O Goddess of the lords of gods, there is no doubt that the water of the Gaṅgā is the cause that grants liberation among all castes, as well as the generator of heaven and other realms.
O Goddess, the supreme power Mahākālī dwells in the *kāraṇa*;
O Supreme Sovereign, the Great Vidyā dwells eternally in the wine.
She who takes the form of the fifty letters dwells eternally in the great conch.
By the power of the Great Vidyā, O beloved, one is always and forever absorbed into the Great Conch; by the mere touch of the Gaṅgā, one dissolves into the Gaṅgā,
just as fire exists in wood or grass merely by touching them.
O Goddess, beloved, just as one who touches the Gaṅgā is absorbed into the Gaṅgā at that very moment, so too, O Supreme Lady,
Mahāśaṅkha becomes like a piece of wood within the stone machine, the Tulasī plant, and other such objects; of this there is no doubt.

The supreme practitioner who recites [the mantra] on a rosary known as the *mahāśaṅkha* holds the eight supernatural powers (*aṣṭasiddhi*) in his hand; he alone is the imperishable Śambhu. For him upon whose head the Gaṅgā resides, what need is there for bathing in the Gaṅgā?
Vārāṇasī, Kāmarūpa, Haridvāra, Prayāgaka,
the Gaṇḍakī, Badarikā, O Goddess, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean—
by the mere sight of him who has devotion for Mahāśaṅkha, these [are attained].
One obtains the entire fruit of bathing at sacred fords; there is no doubt in this matter.
Thus has everything most difficult to attain been told to you, my beloved.
O Supreme Goddess, it must not be spoken in the presence of an uninitiated person, even at the cost of one's life.
In the *Mātṛkābhedatantra*,
the fifth chapter,
the venerable Caṇḍikā said:
"O Śaṅkara, by what means is mercury (pārada) transformed into ash?
I wish to hear that, if you have compassion for me.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Pārvatī, various obstacles arise in the preparation of mercury-ash (pāradabhasman);

therefore, at the outset of that process, the best of the twice-born should perform a rite of pacification (śānti). He should select an officiant for the ritual according to the procedure to be described hereafter.
O Daughter of the Mountain, one should worship the sixteen earthen liṅgas with the sixteen-fold service according to the procedure taught by Toḍala;
O Goddess of the Gods, the honey-mixture (madhuparka) fit for enjoyment should be offered.
One should bathe the Lord of Gods with the five nectars and pure water;
one should offer a pair of garments suitable for the person.
A silver pedestal four fingers wide [should also be provided].
One should offer appropriate ornaments to the person;
or, O Auspicious One, one should give sandalwood paste mixed with lac-dye.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should offer the six-limbed incense again and again.
Likewise, for the sake of auspiciousness, one should offer a lamp filled with ghee;
one should present various delightful food offerings accompanied by many kinds of fruits,
having prepared milk-rice mixed with sugar.
O Maheśānī, O beloved, one should offer water mixed with Vijayā.
The best of practitioners should then recite the great six-syllable mantra a thousand times more than the number of Gajāntakas; thereafter, he will certainly attain perfection.
Alternatively, O Supreme Goddess, one should worship Dhanadā, the bestower of wealth,
with great effort through the sixteen modes of service.
The wise practitioner should perform sacrifice for twelve days and then recite the mantra a thousand times.
O Maheśānī, the wise practitioner should perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*) consisting of one-tenth of that [number].
O Goddess, if he is unable to perform the ritual of *homa* and so forth, he should perform twice the number of recitations (*japa*).
For if she becomes pleased, what then would not be accomplished?
O Supreme Goddess, every day Kubera bestows wealth;
O Śivā, what wonder is there for him regarding the production of sacred ash, O Goddess?
One should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the Guru according to the extent of one's means.
Then the practitioner of mantra shall become a Siddha; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"O Lord of the Gods, [tell me] the procedure for the rite of preparing the sacred ash."
"O Lord, by whom this form, once performed, is reduced to ashes," [the Lord] said. Śrī Śaṅkara replied:
"O Goddess, having brought mercury, one should place it upon a stone."
Upon that, one should recite the mantra consisting of nine syllables, which is worthy of universal veneration.
O Goddess of gods, the foremost of practitioners should recite it one thousand and eight times over a cloth resembling the color of dawn, joined with *syayambhu* flowers.
O Goddess Śivā, having placed the mercury in a pair of earthen vessels,
one should bind it with great effort using a thread adorned with flowers.
O Supreme Sovereign, [one should do this] with water from the stream of liberation over the grain.
One should apply [the paste] with great effort and allow it to dry during the Raudra [muhūrta];
then the wise one should apply it again and subsequently cast it into the fire.
O Queen of the Gods, one should never cast it on the eighth or ninth nights.
Alternatively, O Supreme Goddess, one should place the mercury in an earthen vessel;
that substance should be purified with great effort using the juice of the creeper (vallī).
In the same way, one should perform the purification using the juice of a woman (ghṛtanārī).
When this has been done, if the pill should be firmly bound,
one should bring *dhustūra* and make its center hollow;
likewise, it should be combined with the *tulasī* known as *kṛṣṇā* and *ghṛtakumārikā*.
When the fire-union (*vahni-yoga*) is performed in this manner, it is said that [the substance] is reduced to ashes;
through the grace of Dhanada, gold is produced from the ash-union (*bhasma-yoga*).
If one does not perform worship, the material becomes discolored.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
O Lord, what is the self-arisen (*svayambhu*) like? And what is the *kuṇḍagola* like?
O Lord, what is the "flower of one's own" (*svapuṣpa*) like? And what is the "vajra-flower" (*vajrapuṣpa*) like?
"O Lord Śaṅkara, tell me, what is the nature of that which arises at all times?
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"A maiden who has not yet been married, when she first becomes possessed of menses—"
O Maheśānī, that blood is *svayambhū* (self-arisen); of this there is no doubt.
O Śivā, when a husband is present, the maiden born of another [man] is likewise;
that which arises from her is *kuṇḍapuṣpa*, which accomplishes the purpose of all undertakings.
O Goddess of gods, O Śivā, when her husband has died, the *golapuṣpa* produced by a maiden born of another [man] is supremely effective for subjugating the gods; likewise,
[the substance] from the first occurrence of menstruation in a married maiden [is so].
O Maheśānī, that blood is one's own flower, which deludes all. If a flower arises from the striking of a married maiden or a man, that is proclaimed as the *vajra*.
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, it is said that for a married maiden, whatever occurs every month is the flower arising at all times;
one should place it with great effort in the midst of a fire accompanied by loud cries.
Then, having risen and placed that substance in a golden vessel, O Supreme Goddess, one should recite the great mantra known as Prāsāda.
Thereby the practitioner of mantra becomes perfected; it is not otherwise, as I have spoken.
O Maheśānī, having recited this mantra one thousand times— the same as the number of Gajāntakas—
one should thereafter worship the earthen Śivaliṅga.
Then, O beloved of my life, listen as the examination must be performed.
Pure copper, measured at one *tolaka*, should be placed in a clay vessel in the midst of fire. O Supreme Goddess,
if one should cast [the mercury] measuring a *guñjā* into that molten copper,
it will certainly become gold at that very moment.
If one consumes that substance in the measure of a *guñjā* berry as food,
one becomes free from all diseases and becomes like the god of love (*Madana*);
for such a person, there shall be the perfection of mantras and the attainment of long life.

O Supreme Goddess, if one should enjoy a hundred women every day, he would not be deprived of virility and other qualities; it is the supreme means for increasing vital energy. I see no death at all for him, provided he remains absorbed in meditation.
Upon seeing his wealth, even Kubera was surpassed;
Tumburu himself was eclipsed by his singing, and Vāsava by his generosity—
just as the lord of yoga is surpassed by Maheśa, and Durdhara by Nirṛti.
Possessing great strength, great heroism, and great courage, he is pure, exceedingly translucent, compassionate, and devoted to the welfare of all living beings.
O Goddess, what more need be said? He alone is the leader of the host.
The Mātṛkābhedatantra, Chapter Six.
The venerable Caṇḍikā said:
Speak, O Īśāna, omniscient one, best among those who know all principles!
[Speak] regarding great disease, great suffering, the crisis of great poverty,
or even when various illnesses have arisen, or in the crisis of various afflictions and the like.
In the event of the loss of a kingdom, fear of the king, or being imprisoned;
likewise, O Lord of Gods, in the case of punishment by the state or affliction by the planets—by what means, O Lord of Gods, is one liberated? Tell me, O Śaṅkara.
The illustrious Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs and good fortune, to that which you ask me;
I shall explain all of it to you—pay close attention and understand it well.
"What on earth cannot be accomplished merely by the application of this primordial, supreme Vidyā, Cāmuṇḍā, the transcendent Kālikā? Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"O Supreme Lord, Rāhu is renowned everywhere as a Caṇḍāla;
O God, how can there be a time of merit (puṇyakāla) upon his touching the sun, and likewise, O Lord, upon the moon? This is the doubt in my heart."
"Speak, O Parānanda; afterwards, reveal something else.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs, O fortunate one, to this most excellent of all graspings."
O Goddess, the grasping is threefold, joined with the Moon, the Sun, and Fire. Fire always resides in the eye on the forehead of Śakti;
likewise, the Moon is in the left eye, and the Sun is established in the right.
O Queen of the Gods, when Śambhunātha performs the act of lovemaking,
at that very moment, O Goddess, there is an eclipse, since Śiva is then united with Śakti.
When there is a kiss upon the left eye, then there is an eclipse of the moon.
Then, when there is a kiss on the right eye, there is an eclipse of the sun;
O Supreme Goddess, when there is a kiss on the forehead, there is an eclipse of fire.
Since fire is the seed of Śiva, it is therefore invisible, O Mistress of the Gods.
Rāhu is declared to be Śiva, and Śakti is said to consist of the three qualities (guṇas).
O Supreme Goddess, the union of Śiva and Śakti is the "seizing" (grahaṇa).
O Dear One, the union of Śiva and Śakti is Time consisting of Brahman.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, one should not deliberate upon the zodiac signs and so forth.
O Parameśvarī, only when there is a conjunction through the lunar day, asterism, and yoga,
O Parameśānī, should one perform the calculation of the zodiac signs and the rest.
Through the union of Śiva and Śakti, the entire world consists of Brahman;
O Supreme Goddess, one should not utter the names of months, fortnights, or lunar days.
By merely looking [upon it], it should be recited as a mantra, and then success will certainly be attained.
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, that time should be known as the supreme time.
Whatever is performed there, all of it is said to yield infinite fruit.
Everything has already been told; why say more now?
Indeed, this most secret distinction has been revealed out of affection for you;
it must not be spoken before an uninitiated person (paśu), O Goddess of the Gods.
This reality is known with effort by Brahmā and Mādhava.
"It must be guarded with great effort, O Daughter of the Mountain, as if it were one's own birthplace.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"O Supreme Lord, what is the nature of the great mantra of Cāmuṇḍā?"
"O treasure-house of compassion, tell me what kind of propitiation that is.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"Listen, O lady of beautiful limbs, O fortunate one, to the supreme mantra of Cāmuṇḍā."
By the mere knowledge of which, there is no further rebirth.
O Goddess, the pair of *kāli* seeds, followed by the *kūrca* seed—
this three-syllabled supreme Vidyā is Cāmuṇḍā herself, Kālikā.
For seven days one should worship the Goddess with the sixteen types of offerings;
at the conclusion of the worship, O fair-faced one, one should recite the mantra three thousand times.
At night, however, one should worship the Supreme Goddess with the five principles (pañcatattva).
Likewise, one should recite the mantra at night, accompanied by the Kula-śakti.
One should provide a very spacious pedestal suitable for the construction of the yantra,
and an appropriate offering of madhuparka fit for enjoyment should be presented.

O Supreme Goddess, just as a garment should be provided for a young woman according to her capacity, so too should it be given for the sake of all prosperity. One should apply ornaments in their respective places as is appropriate.
One should offer various kinds of delightful food-oblations (naivedya) consisting of diverse ingredients;
meat-based food should be presented, as well as milk-rice (paramānna) with sugar.
Then, one should worship with supreme devotion, followed by the offering of the sacrificial oblation (bali).

O Supreme Goddess, one should offer the *bali* daily, or at the beginning and end [of the day], O Great Goddess; or, once the ritual with its ancillaries has been completed, one may then offer the *bali*.
When this is done, one attains great accomplishment; of this there is no doubt.
One who desires wealth shall obtain wealth; one who desires a son shall possess a son.
In a dispute he attains victory, and at the royal court he shall be triumphant.
Having become victorious everywhere, like the son of a goddess upon the earth, he shall prevail.
Having worshipped [her], one is liberated from terrible diseases;
for him, there shall be the fulfillment of his desires and the attainment of all perfections, and not otherwise.
O Goddess, even one who has been cast into prison is released—of this there is no doubt.
O Supreme Goddess, this practice— the essence that is most difficult to obtain—
has been revealed out of great affection for you in this place, O Mistress of the Gods. Or else, O Supreme Goddess, one should recite the eternal Caṇḍī.
One should worship the goddess Caṇḍikā with fragrant flowers, O Queen of the Gods, along with incense,
lamps, perfumes, and food offerings. One must certainly worship the supreme Caṇḍikā with the five elements (pañcatattva).
O Supreme Goddess, at the beginning, with the hymn beginning with the Ṛṣi and so forth, and at the conclusion of the *arghya* offering,
the one most skilled in the scriptures should bring forth the five principles (*pañcatattva*) and purify them;
then, having performed the libation (*tarpaṇa*), he should cast [the remains] into the *arghya* vessel.
Having sprinkled [the seat] with water for the guest-offering (arghya), one should worship the deity of the seat (pīṭhadevatā).
Having uttered the Praṇava, and after that the Māyā-bīja,
[one worships] Prabhā, Māyā, Jayā, Sūkṣmā, Viśuddhā, and likewise Nandinī.
One should worship Suprabhā, Vijayā, and Sarvasiddhidā;
then, ending with "vajranakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāya hūṃ phaṭ," O Goddess of Gods, one should worship the seat with the word "namas" at the end.
Having worshipped the lineage of gurus, one should again perform meditation.
Then, having performed the invocation, the mudrās, the placement of the vital breath (jīvanyāsa), and the worship,
and having worshipped with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), one should worship the retinue.

The best of practitioners should worship the Śaṅkha-nidhi and the Padma-nidhi, as well as Brāhmī and the others; he should also honor Indra and the other deities, along with their weapons such as the thunderbolt (vajra),
using the formula beginning with *praṇava* (oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*.

Furthermore, O Maheśānī, one should worship the Goddess with the five principles (*pañcatattva*). Then, having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), and having meditated upon the oneness of the Guru, the mantra, and the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*), O Queen of the Gods, one should recite the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) one hundred times.
Then, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), one should collect the ingredients beginning with the *kāraṇa*.
Having offered it to her and drunk some oneself, O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite the Caṇḍī.
When the Māhātmya has been completed along with its ancillaries, one should perform the drinking again.
Then the wise man should recite [the mantra] in sequence and perform the drinking;
when it is completed, he should again mutter the mantra one hundred times in reverse order.
O Goddess, if by the power of fortune a man should obtain union with Śakti, [he should do so].
At that very moment, one should know that all success rests in the palm of one's hand; O Great Goddess, if one performs the recitation after having done this,
what can I possibly say regarding the majesty of that recitation?
Even if one were to have a hundred mouths, O Queen of Gods, it would still not be possible to describe it;
how much less, then, can it be described now by one with five mouths? O Queen of Gods, by reciting this but once, what more need be said of the absolute Brahman?
O Supreme Goddess, one will certainly obtain peace everywhere;
if one does not obtain peace, then my word is false.
One should first perform the worship with the sixteen-fold service (ṣoḍaśopacāra).

O Dear One, in the second [chapter], one should worship Caṇḍikā with the five principles (pañcatattva). O Goddess of Gods, the fruit that a man obtains by reciting [the text] a thousand times does not equal even a sixteenth part of the fruit of a single recitation.
I shall now declare her meditation, by meditating upon which a person may recite [this mantra]:
*Oṃ! She who is Caṇḍī, the destroyer of Daityas such as Madhu and Kaiṭabha; she who maddens Mahiṣa; she who crushes Dhūmrekṣaṇa, Caṇḍa, and Muṇḍa; she who devours Raktabīja;

she who is the Śakti who destroys the Daityas Śumbha and Niśumbha; she who is the supreme Lakṣmī of Siddhi—that Goddess, the Sovereign of the Universe, accompanied by her nine crores of forms, may she protect me!* (MBhT 6.56–57)
Listen, O you who are honored by heroes, to this meditation of Caṇḍikā.
Listen as I shall proclaim the mantra, which is difficult to obtain even in the three worlds:
first the beginning of the Veda (Om), then the source of speech (Aiṃ), then Māyā (Hrīṃ), and after that the seed-syllable of desire (Klīṃ).
"O Dear One, at the beginning one should recite the nine-syllable great mantra— sthiramāyā, mahāmāyā, the seed-syllable of desire (kāmabīja), and then *namaḥ*— one hundred times.
At the end of the recitation, however, one should recite the great mantra in reverse order one hundred times."
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the seers (*ṛṣi*) and the meters (*chandas*), which are very difficult to obtain.

*Oṃ*. For this great hymn of seven hundred verses (*saptaśatī-mahāstotra*), Medhātithi is the seer; the Gāyatrī, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī are the meters; Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, and Mahāsarasvatī are the deities; *aiṃ*, *hrīṃ*, *klīṃ* are the seed-syllables (*bīja*); and *kṣrauṃ* is the weapon-syllable (*astra*).
"Oṃ, this is my *viniyoga* for the sake of accomplishing my desire, [namely] such-and-such.
O Maheśānī, one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the *praṇava*.
Thus, O beloved, the characteristics of the recitation of the Caṇḍī have been told to you."

"Sārvaṇiḥ Sūrya," and so forth—O Goddess, one should recite just this much, neither more nor less. O Goddess, having performed the ritual recitation (*japa*) for three days, one should recite it three times [daily]. In cases of a great disease accompanied by suffering, or in terrible afflictions such as royal oppression, [this should be done].
Whether one is afflicted by various diseases, or faces the destruction of a kingdom, or likewise fear;

when tormented by planetary influences and the like, or fallen into the sin of killing a Brahmin and so forth—by reciting [this] thus, O Goddess of gods, one is liberated; there is no doubt in this matter.
O Goddess, what need is there for much speaking? A man shall obtain all peace;
liberated from all doubt, he becomes like Madana himself.
O Maheśānī, if success does not arise even when this has been performed in this way, [then the mantra is ineffective].
It must be performed again by that very same person; thereafter, success will certainly be attained.
*Mātṛkābhedatantra*, Chapter Seven.
Śrī Śiva said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully declare the supreme mantra of Tripurā,
by the mere knowledge of which rebirth no longer exists.
O Goddess Śivā, the triple Tripurā was previously declared as Bālā;
likewise, the goddess Bhairavī was described by me in the Nityātantra.
Now, O Pārvatī, listen with respect to the goddess Sundarī.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord, I have heard the great mantra in the Vāmakeśvarayāmala;
O Lord of Gods, now tell me the sequence of worship beginning with the morning rites."

The illustrious Śiva said: Having risen in the morning, the knower of mantras should perform the previously described meditation upon his own guru within the thousand-petaled lotus and worship him with great effort.
And thus, the meditation on the venerable Guru has been described in the *Guptasādhanatantra*.
O fair-faced one, listen now to the mantra which I previously mentioned:
one should utter the seed-syllable of Speech (*vāgbīja*) and Mahāmāyā, the power of Viṣṇu.

Then [one recites] the mantra of Tathānandabhairava: *hasakhaphreṃ*. After that, the mantra of his Śakti; and then likewise, *hasauḥ* is remembered. O Sovereign of the Gods, this is the mantra of the Śrīguru and his Śakti.
After the venerable Guru ending in Ānandanātha, the Śakti is then declared as follows:
having uttered the seed-syllables beginning with Vāk, [one says] "Amukānandanātha," then "Śrīpādukām," and after that, "I worship, obeisance. (MBhT 7.8)
One should utter the seed-syllable of Speech (Vāgbīja), then the Consort of Śambhu, and thereafter the Beloved of Hari.
Having pronounced the seed-syllable of the Elements (Bhūtabīja), one should then say, "O Goddess of Gods, I offer this worship; such is the ritual procedure," O Dear One.
Then one should recite the eight-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times.
Having offered the recitation, O Dear One, one should bow with palms joined in reverence.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, I now wish to hear the hymn of praise and the armor-mantra;
O Master, you previously spoke of the armor-mantra and hymn of the Śrīguru, O Lord.
Now, let the hymn and armor-mantra of the Strīguru be told to me.
"By the mere knowledge of which there is no further rebirth.
Śrī Śiva said:
"Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim this hymn of supreme secrecy."
Merely by hearing it, a person is liberated from saṃsāra.
Homage to you, O Goddess of the gods; homage to you, who are worshipped by Hara.
To her whose very nature is the knowledge of Brahman, eternal salutations, salutations!
Salutations again and again to her by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance has been opened with the collyrium-stick of knowledge;
she is the supreme mother who carries one across the ocean of worldly bondage.
She who is the giver of knowledge, the giver of liberation, and eternal—to her, eternal salutations again and again.

(MBhT 7.17) She who dwells on the left side of the Lord, who is always worshipped by the gods, and who is the constant bestower of higher wisdom—to her, eternal salutations again and again. (MBhT 7.18)
To her who resides in the thousand-petaled great lotus, whose nature is eternal bliss,
the goddess who bestows supreme liberation— to her, constant salutations, salutations! She who is the embodiment of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and the embodiment of Mahārudra.
And she whose essential nature consists of the three *guṇas*; to her, eternal salutations again and again!
(MBhT 7.20) And she who has the form of the moon, the sun, and fire, with eyes perpetually rolling;
having embraced her own Lord, to her, eternal salutations again and again! (MBhT 7.21)

Salutations again and again to her who bestows liberation while living (jīvanmukti) through the states of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others, and who grants both knowledge (jñāna) and realized wisdom (vijñāna). O Maheśānī, whoever recites this hymn endowed with devotion, [attains the supreme goal].
He attains success constantly; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
He who recites it at dawn, preceded by worship of the Guru, is indeed blessed in this world like the son of a goddess upon the earth.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Queen of the Gods, the hymn of praise is completed; now listen with reverence to the armor (kavaca), by the mere hearing of which one attains equality with the Lord of Speech.
Sadāśiva is remembered as the seer (ṛṣi) of this armor-mantra (kavaca) of the female preceptor;
the deity is declared to be the one named after that [mantra], bestowing the fruits of the four aims of life.
May "klīṃ," the seed-syllable, protect my head; that which is proclaimed as such protects the forehead.
May the seed-syllable *klīṃ* protect my two eyes; may it always protect all my limbs.
May the seed-syllable *aiṃ* protect my face; may *hrīṃ* protect my shanks.
May the seed-syllable *śrīṃ* protect the region of my shoulders; may the seed-syllable of speech (*vāgbhava*) protect my two arms.

May the letter *ha* protect my right arm, the letter *kṣa* my left hand, and the letter *kṣma* below them; may the letter *la* protect my heart. May the letter *ra* protect the region of my back, and the letter *ra* my right side.
May the syllable *jūṃ* protect my left side, and the syllable *sa*, Meru itself;
may the syllable *ma* protect my fingers, and the syllable *la* my nails. May the syllable *va* protect my hips, and the syllable *ra* my pair of knees.
May the syllable *yīḥ* protect the pair of feet, while *hasauḥ* protects every limb;
may *hasauḥ* protect the genitals, the body hair, and the hair of the head.
May the seed-syllable *aiṃ* protect in the east, and may the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* protect in the south.
May the seed-syllable *Śrīṃ* protect [me] in the west, and that which originates from the elements (*bhūtasambhava*) in the north.
May *Śrīṃ* protect me in the southeast, and may that which bears its name protect me in the southwest.
May the Mother Goddess (*devy ambā*) protect me in the northwest, as well as the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Śambhu.
"I worship [thee] above, and likewise I bow below; may [Thou] protect me always.
Thus, O beloved, I have told you this most wonderful armor (kavaca).
If one recites the armor after having muttered the guru-mantra, [it shall grant protection].

He is a perfected one (siddha), and he along with his retinue is Śiva himself; of this there is no doubt. O Goddess of the Gods, for whoever recites this armor (kavaca), which is the embodiment of mantras, at the time of worship, the fruit of that worship shall be his; this is the truth, the absolute truth.

O Goddess, he who recites this at the three junctions of the day becomes a perfected one; of this there is no doubt. If one writes it on birch bark, places it inside a pill, and wears it while it is encased in gold, then by the mere sight of him, the disputants are rendered lusterless.
In dispute he attains victory, and in battle he is like Nirṛti;
in an assembly he attains victory, for he is my equal—of this there is no doubt.
If one should recite this while meditating on that [wheel] with a thousand spokes at the three junctions of the day, [he shall succeed].
That very one, having attained perfection as Lokeśa, seeks the state of Nirvāṇa.
This armor known as Samastamaṅgala is most wonderful;
it must never be given to just anyone, nor should it ever be disclosed.
It should be given to a disciple who is tranquil; otherwise, a downfall will occur.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should not reveal this even to sons who lack devotion.
Whoever recites the tenfold vidyā without knowing this armor (kavaca), [will meet with misfortune].
He does not obtain the fruit thereof, and others shall go to hell.
O Goddess, the armor is complete; what else do you wish to hear?
Out of the bond of affection for you, what is there that I have not revealed?
O Dear One, having uttered the *kūrca* seed-syllable and then the *prāṇa* mantra,
one should cause the *kuṇḍalinī* wheel to move by means of this application of air.
Having recited the root mantra one hundred and eight times, the wise practitioner should bow down.
Then, having performed the rite of bathing, one should perform the twilight devotion (saṃdhyā) as previously described.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"O Supreme Lord, tell me: what is the nature of the meditation for the twilight devotion?"
"O Lord, let the specific [instruction] regarding Śrīvidyā be told to me.
Śrīśiva said:
"One should meditate upon the goddess Sundarī, who is threefold and whose form consists of seed-syllables (bīja)."
At dawn, one should worship the Goddess as Vāgbhavā; at midday, as the essence of Madana;
and in the evening, as Śakti. At the time of worship, one should meditate upon the Great Goddess Śivā, who is threefold and whose form is the Bindu, according to her specific nature.
One should contemplate the Vāgbhava [seed-syllable] as being moon-like and white in color;
one should visualize the Śakti-bīja as golden-colored and red in hue.
At dawn, it has the luster of white, and at midday, it resembles blue.
In the evening, the best of practitioners should meditate on her as having a red-colored luster.
O Great Goddess, having meditated thus, the wise one should perform the twilight ritual (saṃdhyā).
Then, having performed the worship of Śiva, he should worship the Supreme Deity.
Then one should worship the goddess Tripurā, the bestower of liberation;
Tripurā is the supreme knowledge, the great knowledge,
and the devoted wife who never accepts worship that is devoid of worship of her husband.
Therefore, O Maheśānī, one should first worship the Liṅga;
one should worship the five-faced [deity] with the five-syllabled mantra with great effort.
Thereafter, one should worship the Goddess Tripurā, the bestower of liberation.
The Goddess said:
O Śaṅkara, out of compassion, tell me upon what support one should worship Śambhu;
for, O Lord of Gods, according to the difference in the support, the practitioner shall become a partaker of the fruit.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Goddess, one should worship [the Lord] in an earthen liṅga, as well as in a stone liṅga,
or in a liṅga made of gold, silver, copper, or bell-metal.
One should worship [the deity] in mercury, or in the Gaṅgā, or in a crystal or emerald linga;
according to the specific purpose, one may worship in a linga made of iron, a linga fashioned from ashes,
a linga made of sand, or even one made of cow dung.
O Goddess, I have described the worship of the earthen [liṅga] in the tradition known as Toḍala.
O Goddess, one should not worship [the deity] on stone or other materials without performing the consecration (*saṃskāra*).
I shall now explain that consecration, along with whatever specificities apply here.
Having placed a silver and a golden linga into a golden vessel,
one should lift that linga out from there and immerse it in milk for three days;
then, having installed it with the Tryambaka mantra, one should worship Kālarudra.
One should worship Pārvatī upon the altar with the sixteen-fold ritual service.
Therefore, having lifted that *liṅga* from the waters of the Gaṅgā for three days,
the wise man should then perform the consecration according to the procedure prescribed in the Vedas.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"O Lord of gods, O Master, tell me the measurement of the liṅga;
and whether there be any distinction between those made of earth, stone, and so forth."
The illustrious Śiva said:
One *tolaka* of clay should be taken, or perhaps two *tolakas*;
other than this, it should never be done, O Pārvatī.
O Parameśānī, [an image] made of stone and so forth yields gross results;
O Deveśī, it may be the size of a thumb or the size of a mountain of gold.
In this manner, O Deveśī, one shall obtain manifold fruits in due order.
O Supreme Goddess, the rudrākṣa is a liṅga more gross than the gross;
O Goddess, it is taught that manifold fruits result from its worship and wearing. (Mātṛkābhedatantra 7.68–69)
The Eighth Chapter.
The Śrī Devī said:
Listen, O Lord, supreme bliss, whose nature is both the transcendent and the immanent Kula!
In my knowledge, no protector exists other than you, O Maheśāna. The perfect *liṅga* is the seed of Śiva and not otherwise;
likewise, within the stone is the supreme wheel of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
"O Mahādeva, even a hundredth part of mercury does not exist within my knowledge;
it is the seed of Śiva, the very form of Śiva, and not otherwise.
O Lord, tell me how it can have the form of a *liṅga*, O Master."
Śrī Śiva said:
Just as my Liṅga composed of light exists upon the peak of Kailāsa,
so too Viśveśvara stands in Kāśī, being a single sixteenth part of that very same [Liṅga].
O Maheśānī, the complete liṅga is the seed of Śiva and nothing else;
likewise, within the stone is the supreme Cakra, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
Indeed, even a hundredth part of mercury does not constitute Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
The letter *pa* is the form of Viṣṇu, and likewise the letter *ā* is Kālikā;
the letter *repha* (ra) is Śiva, and the letter *da* is the form of Brahmā, not otherwise.
O Supreme Goddess, mercury (*pārada*) consists of the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
He who worships the mercury-liṅga is indeed the imperishable Śambhu;
he alone is blessed, O Goddess of gods, he is the man of knowledge, and he is the knower of reality.
He is the knower of Brahman, he is wealthy, and he is a king honored upon the earth.
The supreme practitioner is the lord of powers such as *aṇimā* and the rest.
Women are fickle by nature; indeed, they cannot be guarded.
For this very reason, O Goddess of gods, O Pārvatī, desist from this.
The Goddess said:
"Speak, O Lord of Compassion, if there is mercy within you;
for without your word, O God, where is liberation and where is goodness?"
The illustrious Śiva said:
Mercury is indeed the seed of Śiva; one must certainly not subject it to beating (*tāḍana*).
From beating there would be loss of wealth, and from beating there would be the loss of sons.
"From striking [the deity], one may become afflicted by disease; from striking, death may occur.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"O Lord, these obstacles and so forth are indeed true; there is no doubt about this."
"O Lord, O ocean of compassion, tell me how [the practice] may be free from obstacles and the like.
Śrī Śiva said:
"O Śivā, since there are various obstacles in the preparation of pārada (mercury)."
Therefore, at the very beginning, one should perform rites for peace and well-being there.
The twelfth is the earthen linga, which should be fashioned with the sixteen types of offerings,
or made from materials such as silk cloth or thread, and colored white.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should offer a pair of garments suitable for the man,
and the honey-mixture (madhuparka) appropriate for enjoyment should be given;
one should also give ornaments according to one's ability for the sake of auspiciousness.
O Pārvatī, one should worship with great effort using *bilva* leaves;
according to the rite spoken by Toḍala, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times for each leaf.
First, one should recite the five-syllabled mantra one hundred and eight times.
At the conclusion of the worship, he should then mutter the great mantra known as Prāsāda;
having performed the rites ending with the sacrificial fee, he should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya) with his senses subdued.
He should never, under any circumstances, avoid betel-leaf or fish.
In this tantra, one should offer sacrificial food, betel, and excellent fish;
O Supreme Goddess, one should perform the oblation in the tenth or hundredth part [of the recitation].
A fee for the oblation must be given, and then one is not defiled by obstacles.
Then, on the following day, the wise practitioner should bring mercury;
over it, he should recite the mantra consisting of nine syllables that are worthy of universal veneration:
the seed-syllable of space (ha), ending with Śiva (kṣa), followed by the first letter of the consonant class (ka), with a bindu upon its head.
O Dear One, O Maheśānī, one should recite this mantra— consisting of the seed-syllable of Vāyu, the triad, and the triad [forming] Tryambaka— over the medicinal herb;
if one recites the mantra over the mercury one hundred and eight times.
That very [substance] becomes bound by means of medicinal application, and not otherwise.
Then, on the following day, O beloved of my life, listen:
one should choose a performer of the rite according to the extent of one's stated wealth.
One should offer gold in the shape of a campaka flower upon the pair of ears;
and upon the neck, one should place a very beautiful gold ornament consisting of four corners, O Maheśānī. One should give a pair of bracelets on both hands.
A bracelet of white color and likewise a ring;
one should offer a wave-patterned yellow cloth and a pair of linen garments, O Śivā.
Having done this, O Maheśānī, one should meditate upon the form of Śiva.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the procedure; listen, O Pārvatī.
Having placed [the substance] upon a grinding stone and mixing it with the juice of the *jhiṇṭī* leaf, one should stir it with the grinding stone until it becomes like mud, my dear.
O beautiful goddess, if it should be suitable for transformation right there, then,
having fashioned that *liṅga*,
one should make it even more firm with one's own flowers, cloth, charcoal, and dried cow-dung.
It should be made slightly warm so that it becomes more solid;
then, having fashioned that linga, one should make it even firmer again,
and place it upon an earthen vessel covered with one's own flowers.
It should be made somewhat warm until it becomes firmer;
for without the application of medicinal substances, it turns to ash and not otherwise. *Mātṛkābhedatantra* 8.34.
The Ninth Chapter.
Śrī Śiva said:
O Goddess, beloved of my life-breath, listen to the method for preparing the sacred ash.
First, one should choose a performer according to the extent of one's stated wealth.
One should present gold together with pearls upon the pair of ears,
as well as bracelets and likewise rings upon the pair of hands.
One should cause two armlets made of pure gold to be placed upon the pair of arms,
and on the neck, one should place beautiful four-cornered gold ornaments;
likewise, a pair of very splendid garments made of silk thread.

The *uṣṇīṣa* is white in color, and the *uṣṇīṣa* is clad in yellow garments. Thus, O Goddess, one should choose [the deity] suitable for the rite; one should contemplate the form of Śiva and contemplate him as consisting of the three qualities (*triguṇātmaka*).
Then, on the following day, O beautiful one, one should perform rites for peace and prosperity (*śāntisvastyayana*).
Having fashioned [an image] out of pure gold and a *bilva* leaf, O Goddess,
one should worship twelve earthen [images] by the number of a thousand.
With the sixteen-fold service and a pair of silk garments,
one should worship the Supreme Lord with various ornaments;
one should offer that which is fit for enjoyment and present the *madhuparka*.
Having established [the deities] upon golden seats, one should perform the worship for each individually.
At the conclusion of the worship, the wise person should mutter the mantra one hundred and eight times—
the great six-syllabled mantra known as Prāsāda.
One should recite the mantra ten thousand times, O beloved, and perform oblations amounting to one-tenth of that number.
O Goddess of gods, O mistress of the supreme lord, hear from me, O you who are dear as my own life, regarding the substance for the oblation;
it may be performed even in a sacrificial pit constructed of sand, O Supreme Goddess.
O Beloved, one should construct a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) with auspicious characteristics, measuring thirty-two finger-breadths in width and the same in depth; indeed,
O Śivā, O Supreme Goddess, above that, it should be four finger-breadths [in height].
Thus, with a golden pitcher that is not inferior to a copper one,
he should place either of these two pitchers upon the altar,
having carefully wrapped it with a pair of silk cloths.
O Goddess of the gods, one should perform the oblation with bilva leaves according to the prescribed method, smeared with the three sweets; then one will certainly become accomplished.
Thereafter, a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be given according to one's stated means.
One should cause to be given a price consisting of all kinds of goods, or even double that amount.
Sacrifices devoid of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) grant neither spiritual perfection nor liberation;
therefore, O Maheśānī, the fee should be according to one's wealth.
O beautiful one, having brought mercury (pārada) equal in weight to a boar's bristle, even at the very moment of birth,
one should consume it with great effort in the measure of one *tolaka*.
Thereafter, one should likewise consume mother’s milk in the measure of one *tolaka*.
Furthermore, the wise one should consume [the substance], and thereafter he should consume milk.
Then, O Goddess of the Gods, having brought forth the calf, he should diligently bind it at the nine gates by means of the application of thread.

Then, O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite the *helakī* mantra one hundred and eight times. The wise practitioner, O Goddess, should fill a trench measuring the size of an elephant and one *prastha* in depth with dried cow dung.
One should place the calf in the middle of that and burn it with great effort.
O Maheśānī, while the fire is present, one must not touch the excellent pit (kuṇḍa).
Once the pit has become thoroughly cooled, one should lift [the calf] out with great effort.
One should recite the all-illuminating mantra one hundred and eight times.
O Pārvatī, listen with respect as I shall proclaim the Lord of the Universe (Viśveśvara):
one should smear a measure of one *tolaka* of mercury onto a copper vessel.
O Maheśānī, one should prepare a powder of one *tolaka* of sulfur;
O Parameśvarī, having carefully covered it with the powder,
one should burn it with great effort using a very gentle fire.
O beautiful one, having seen it black in color and covered in dust, one should raise it up;
O beautiful one, if one should consume that substance for the duration of a night,
truly, truly, every form of leprosy shall go to destruction through its consumption.
Warm water should be used as a post-drink, and one should avoid fish and similar foods.
O Goddess of the Gods, a householder with sons should not perform such a rite;
for on the first day it destroys sons, and on the second day it destroys wealth.
On the third day there is power; on the fourth day, one's home;
on the fifth day, disease; but on the sixth, destruction certainly occurs.
Therefore, O Great Goddess, one should perform rites for one's own well-being.
The practitioner of mantra should perform [the rite] fourfold according to the previously stated procedure.
(Mātṛkābhedatantra, Chapter Ten)
The Goddess said: O Lord, tell me how there can be oneness between the Guru who has a human form, the mantra consisting of phonemes, and the deity who conforms to the object of meditation? MBhT 10.1
Śrī Śiva said:
The supreme mantra is obtained by the best of practitioners from the mouth of the Guru;
if even one [mantra] becomes potent, its form will certainly manifest.
O Dear One, the body of the deity arises from the seed-syllable;
furthermore, another form is born in accordance with the command of the Guru.
O Goddess, through the contemplation of the Guru and others, the perfection of the state arises.
For this very reason, O Great Goddess, unity is proclaimed.
The Śrīdevī said:
O Mahādeva, one should contemplate that which is visual as its source.
"O Mahādeva, what kind of meditation could there be for that which is beyond the range of sight?
Śrī Śiva said:
"O Goddess, that which consists of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman) has issued forth from my mouth."
O Goddess, just as meditation and other practices may occur even for one devoid of formal forms, so too [the goal is attained] through mere recitation with a mind endowed with devotion.
This is the truth, the absolute truth, O Great Mistress; it is directly perceived here, there is no doubt.
The Goddess said:
"O Śaṅkara, tell me what kind of speech is used in the granting of cattle,
by which speech, O Lord of Gods, even the Goddess herself becomes pleased."
The illustrious Śiva said: O Supreme Goddess, one should not apply the word "paśu" (beast) to a deer, a buffalo, a camel, a goat, a lion, or a tiger.

Having applied the word "paśu" (animal), one should offer it to Mahādevī. If the practitioner, remaining in the state of *paśubhāva*, offers a buffalo as a sacrifice (*bali*), the offering should be performed; however, the person [who performs it] must not eat the meat.
O beloved, one does not obtain the perfect fruit; one obtains only a tenth part.
O sweet-spoken one, he who abides by the Divine Hero’s doctrine should offer buffaloes and the like;
only he attains perfection and the full fruit.
O Goddess, one should never perform worship without the gift of an animal;
likewise, if a man is capable of performing the daily worship,
he becomes perfected solely through the offering of the bali-oblation, and not otherwise.
O Supreme Goddess, if one who is destitute should perform worship and other rites,
O Sovereign of the Gods, a single bali offering must be presented at the end of the year;
otherwise, there will be no accomplishment even from worshipping throughout one's entire life.
O Caṇḍikā, in the Kali age, the great sacrifice of *balidāna* exists;
O Sovereign of the Gods, sacrifices such as the horse-sacrifice (*aśvamedha*) do not exist in the Kali age.
Merely by the offering of a *bali*, the fruit of the horse-sacrifice shall be obtained.
Whatever substance remains from a sacrifice is to be eaten, and not otherwise.
By consuming what remains from a sacrifice, one becomes a partaker of the sacrifice; of this there is no doubt.
If, however, one should eat it out of delusion [without having first offered it], one would not share in the fruit of the sacrifice.
O Goddess, how should one offer that substance which is to be abandoned to Mahādevī?
This Great Tantra, whose nature is Brahman, has issued from my mouth;
he who hears even a single syllable of it is purified of all sins.
If one, filled with great devotion, listens to this chapter,
what need has he for meditation or worship, and what need has he for bathing at sacred fords,
O Caṇḍikā, if he knows that everything is composed of the Śabdabrahman?
By mere hearing alone, he becomes perfected; of this there is no doubt.
Whatever fruit is obtained by hearing the eighteen Purāṇas, and whatever fruit is obtained by hearing the four Vedas along with their auxiliary branches, [is attained here].
O Goddess of gods, other tantras do not equal even a sixteenth part of this tantra.
This tantra is the form of Brahman, the essence of essences, higher than the highest. (Mātṛkābhedatantra 10.23–24)
The eleventh chapter.
The venerable Caṇḍikā said:
"If one should offer a temple or even a pavilion to the Goddess,"
O Supreme Lord, tell me its ritual procedure and its greatness.
O Mahādeva, if one should offer a well or similar work to the Goddess,
O Supreme Lord, tell me its ritual procedure and its greatness.
The venerable Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain how one should construct the temple;
on its very western side, one should prepare a square altar (vedikā).
One should perform the wrapping with great effort using a cloth;
O Maheśānī, in its absence, one should wrap it with grass.
Having placed the pair of jars, one should wrap them with a linen cloth.
One should place pairs of linen garments upon each pair of jars.
One should worship the Goddess in the jar of Īśāna, and the deity of Fire in the southeast;
one should worship the chosen deity with the sixty-four types of offerings.
In the absence [of these], one should diligently worship the Goddess with half that amount;
or else, O Supreme Goddess, according to one's capacity and with ritual offerings.
One should worship with great effort, and thereafter perform the fire-oblation (homa) and other rites.
There, one should perform the *kuśaṇḍikā* rite according to the procedure taught in the scriptures.
O Goddess of the gods, the practitioner of mantra should offer oblations with a *bilva* leaf smeared with the three sweets (*trimadhu*);
he should offer a thousand oblations and must not allow them to be less than a hundred.
Then, having offered the *pūrṇāhuti*, one should utter the following words:
"Today," and so forth, pronouncing the solar month;
then the lunar date, the lineage (*gotra*), "I, [name]," and for the sake of virtue, wealth, or desire.
O Supreme Goddess, for the sake of attainment, one should then recite the root mantra.
Afterwards, one should offer salutations to the deity and cause the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) to be given to the guru.
O Mistress of the Gods, one should bathe the patron with the water from the ritual jar.
Having first uttered the *surā* mantras, the wise preceptor should then perform the rite of pacification (*śānti*).
At the very beginning, he should cause the selection (*varaṇa*) of the preceptor-god to be performed.
He should offer gold in the shape of a *campaka* flower to the pair of ears.
One should fasten a four-cornered golden ornament around the neck;
then one should provide a turban and place a garland upon the throat.
Then, a pair of armlets on the arms and bracelets upon the wrists.
A ring should be placed on the finger and divine clothing should be provided;
having thus performed the formal invitation, one should consider [the initiate] fit for the ritual action.
A wise person should diligently invite either the Guru or the Guru’s son.
Indeed, one should not appoint a *sadasya* nor a *tantradhara* there;
nor indeed should one appoint a *brahmā*. One should simply choose a Guru.
O Maheśānī, the servant of the Guru is Bhairava himself—of this there is no doubt.
He himself should satisfy [the preceptor] with his own lower garment;
following the command of the guru, the brahmin should himself become the *hotṛ* priest.
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Māyā, he should say: "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti."

O Goddess, with this mantra one should perform the consecration of the altar (vedisaṃskāra). With the mantra beginning with "bhūr asi" and ending with the weapon-mantra (astra), and with the root-mantra (mūla), one should fasten the turban (uṣṇīṣa) over the pair of jars that have been consecrated.
A wise person should not employ a mantra stated in the Vedas or the Smṛtis;
O Supreme Goddess, this same procedure should be followed for the dedication of wells and other such works.
However, in the case of temples and similar structures, everything else is indeed the same.
One should perform the installation of the well and other structures, and carry out the piercing with a staff.
The piercing in the middle portion should be four cubits in measure;
having uttered the root mantra, one should then place the consort of Fire (Vahni-vadhū).
Then, having raised the staff, the wise man should say, "I am crossing.
At that point, the discerning person must not perform the *dhenu-saṃtaraṇa* (the cow-crossing rite);
by performing the *dhenu-saṃtaraṇa*, a loss of the fruit [of the rite] arises.
One should offer gold, silver, and coral as the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
Having bathed [the image] with water from the jars, the preceptor should then perform the rite of propitiation (*śānti*).
By this very procedure, one should carry out the consecration of wells and other such works.
For by means of this [mantra], one should perform the consecration (utsarga) of ponds, wells, tanks, and the like;
and having diligently offered a long water-channel, a lotus-pool, or any reservoir with supreme devotion to Mahādevī, one should consecrate it by this very [mantra].
O beloved, for seven generations on the father’s side,
and for seven generations on the mother’s side, O dear one,
he shall dwell eternally on Kailāsa by virtue of the boon granted by the Goddess.

He himself is of the very nature of God and is liberated while living; of this there is no doubt. O Goddess, the fruit that one obtains through a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Vājapeya sacrifices becomes a hundred-thousandfold greater than that.
O Goddess of the gods, the fruit one obtains by giving gold equal in weight to Mount Meru to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas is a hundred thousand times greater than that;
[and likewise for giving] the earth with its seven continents, filled with abundant crops.
One should bestow [it] with great effort upon a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, the merit from this is a hundred-thousandfold;
it includes every vow accompanied by sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) and every gift that is in accordance with the Vedas.
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, by this [act], one gains merit a hundred thousand times greater.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
By wearing the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra), one becomes worthy of worship by the world; of this there is no doubt.
"Now, let the procedure for the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra) be told to me.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"O lady of beautiful countenance, hear that which is the measurement of the sacrificial thread."
A follower of the Ṛgveda should wear the thread above the navel and below the breast;
for the measurement of the sacred thread of the Yajus, O Daughter of the Mountain, is indeed marvelous:
the sacrificial thread should be worn by the twice-born according to the measure of the armpits.
One should wear this with effort; never another length, O fair-complexioned one. For the Sāmaga, the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra) is of three kinds:
the sacrificial thread extends from the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) down to the region of the navel.
Alternatively, having placed it upon the neck, one should touch the navel;
from there, extending to the spine and reaching as far as the vertebral column, is the sacrificial thread (*yajñasūtra*).
Or else, O Supreme Goddess, hear another method.
The sacrificial thread should extend from the neck down to the right thumb;
or else, one should carefully wear the thread as prescribed by the Yajurvedins,
or wear it according to the measurement of the Sāmavedins.
The practitioner of the Atharva-veda should wear the sacrificial thread (*yajñasūtra*), which causes supreme delusion;
the sacrificial thread extends from the wheel of command (*ājñācakra*) down to the region of the navel.
Whoever should wear the thread without knowing this secret convention (*saṃketa*)—
O Goddess, he would be equal to a Caṇḍāla even if he were equal to Vyāsa.
*Mātṛkābhedatantra*, Chapter Twelve.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully declare the support for worship, which is very difficult to obtain:
[it may be] in a Śālagrāma stone, a gem, a yantra, an image, a jar, or in water.

In a manuscript, at the Gaṅgā, at a Śiva-liṅga, and at a flower, one obtains a hundredfold fruit; likewise, one obtains that same fruit at a Śālagrāma stone and at a gem. O fair-eyed one, the merit is a hundred-thousandfold at a yantra and a hundred-thousandfold at an image.
O beloved, there is a single unit of merit in a water-pot and a single unit in water;
however, in a manuscript there are a thousand, and at the Gaṅgā the fruit is equal to that. But in a Śiva-liṅga the fruit is indeed infinite, except for the earthen liṅga.
O Maheśānī, by worshipping with a flower-yantra, one partakes in all siddhis;
however, in the worship of a Śālagrāma stone, one should not draw the supreme yantra.
O Maheśānī, when a gem is present, one should not draw the supreme yantra.
And during the worship of the image, one should not draw the supreme yantra. O Supreme Goddess,
having carefully placed a water-pot before the image,
one should worship the retinue there in that pot.
One should worship the deities presiding over the machine within the jar and the machine itself;
one should contemplate the jar as the embodiment of all the deities,
for this jar, O Supreme Goddess, is indeed the very nature of the celestial tree.
If the practitioner should construct a great yantra as the place of origin [of the deity],
he should never, out of delusion, fashion an image there.
If he should fashion an image, however, he must not have a yantra made there.
But if, out of delusion, one should perform it, O beloved, one should worship twice;
there, the offering of the bali should be doubled, the mantra should be recited twice, and the wise man should offer the oblation twice. (MBhT 12.11–12)
"Otherwise, worship is fruitless and the offering of oblations is fruitless;
since everything indeed becomes fruitless, one should not perform the *yantra*.
Thus, O beloved, I have told you that which is the support of worship, so difficult to obtain. (MBhT 12.13–14)
Now, therefore, I shall fully declare the characteristics of the Śiva-liṅga;
by worshipping Śiva in an earthen liṅga, one becomes endowed with all perfections (siddhis).
It is taught that when worshipping Śiva in a stone liṅga, the fruit is twofold.
In worship with a golden liṅga, the destruction of enemies is considered the result;
with one of silver, one becomes the lord of all perfections, and the fruit from that is fourfold.
One should know that with copper there is nourishment, and with bell-metal, an accumulation of wealth.
The greatness of mercury has already been described by me;
in Gaṅgā it is a hundred-thousandfold, but in lac one becomes afflicted with disease.
O beloved, in crystal there is the attainment of all perfections, and likewise in emerald.
In a linga made of iron, there is the destruction of enemies; in a linga made of ashes, the fulfillment of desires.
In one made of sand, there is the attainment of desired objects; in one made of cow dung, the warding off of seasonal afflictions.
Such is the majesty of every linga, which bestows dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
O fair-eyed one, you have been told that the merit which is declared to be superior due to the difference in the substratum is indeed the fruit of this bearer;
O Goddess, by worshipping Śiva, one becomes the master of the four aims of life.

A mortal endowed with the eightfold sovereignty through the worship of Śambhunātha is himself declared to be Nārāyaṇa, if he should fully worship Śambhu. Whatever gods are ever established in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld—

O Goddess, the worship of them occurs through the worship of Śambhunātha. Whatever fruit a man obtains by [offering] a thousand golden flowers, a hundred-thousandfold more merit than that is gained from even a single broken bilva leaf.
The fruit obtained from even a thousand pieces of a single broken bilva leaf cannot be attained even with gold equal in weight to Mount Meru;
furthermore, there is no consideration of purity or impurity in the worship of Śiva.

By worshipping in whatever manner with bilva leaves, that man, having become endowed with all perfections, is indeed a perfected one (siddha). Whatever gods are within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) and whatever deities are outside it—
They all attain satisfaction solely through the worship of Śiva.
One should offer flowers, fragrance, water, and ritual substances upon the liṅga;
within the liṅga is the great fire, which is proclaimed to be Rudra himself.
Whatever one casts upon Rudra, that very thing attains the state of ashes.
O Maheśānī, through the worship of Śiva, there occurs a direct oblation;
through the worship of Śiva, a mortal becomes the lord of the great sacrifice.
O Girijā, if one were to offer even as much water as a drop on the tip of a blade of kusha grass,
that water would indeed truly be equal to the ocean;
and by placing a flower upon the linga, it becomes equal to Mount Meru.
O Goddess, whatever food remains at the top of the *liṅga*,
by the gift of that food one obtains the fruit of gifting the earth.
Even if one should worship the *liṅga* with a single grain of rice, [one gains great merit].
One obtains the fruit of giving food that fills the vessel of the entire universe.
Even by worshipping a Śiva-liṅga with a single blade of dūrvā grass,
one obtains the fruit of offering half of the head of all the gods.
If one were to bathe Maheśvara after bringing him here by way of general analogy,
one would become a partaker of the fruit of bathing at thirty million and a half sacred fords (tīrthas).
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"Tāriṇī is the power (śakti) of Brahmā, while Tripurā is the supreme Vaiṣṇavī.
How is she Śākambharī and Tārā? And how is Tripurā Śāmbhavī? Śrī Śaṅkara said:
When Kālī was born from the body, she became Sāvitrī, the mother of the Vedas;
that goddess is the bestower of the three aims of life and is indeed the power (śakti) of Brahmā.
She is the supreme Śaivī Mahāvidyā of hidden form, Ekajaṭā.
Therefore, she is indeed Lakṣmī, the auspicious consort of Viṣṇu who bestows the three goals of life;
she is the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) in her concealed form, the illustrious Tripurasundarī;
she is the supreme Śāmbhavī Māyā, Tripurā, the giver of liberation.
For there is indeed only one Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), differing only in name;
likewise, the Puruṣa is one, differentiated only by name. Thus spoke the illustrious Caṇḍikā.
"By the mere retention of the mantra, one becomes its very self and absorbed in it;
how then could such a person be afflicted by wind-disorders (vātula), or how could he become diseased?
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
From being concealed by mantra, madness does not arise, nor does disease occur in the body.
O Goddess, listen with a concentrated mind as I shall explain what is concealed by mantra:
lack of devotion, error regarding the syllable, omission, and likewise concealment.

The short and the long, as well as the recitation in dreams, are recorded as being eightfold. Success cannot be attained without devotion even in hundreds of millions of kalpas; likewise, whether it be the mantra or otherwise, one who acts through delusion is a madman.
If a syllable is omitted, there is loss of intellect; if it is broken, there is surely destruction.

With a short pronunciation, one becomes afflicted by disease; with a long recitation, there is loss of wealth. By speaking [the mantra incorrectly], one meets death—even in a dream, O Daughter of the Mountain, hear this.

And the mantra of Kālikā and Tārā is like a blazing fire. O Goddess, if one should steal the mantra through a god in the form of a brahmin with a mind full of affection, listen to the characteristics of such a practitioner (sādhaka).
Flames would surely arise in all his limbs, especially within the center of his body;
likewise, coolness would not be produced in water, nor even through the application of medicinal herbs.
Everything would always be like that of a madman, and even what is perceived would become like a dream.
