Within a year, or within three years, his death will occur; of this there is no doubt.
Śrī Caṇḍikā said:
"I have heard from your mouth the eightfold [system] concealed by mantras."
"O Lord, if by fate it should happen, tell me the means for that.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"Through much recitation, as well as through burnt offerings and the extensive practice of bodily mortification..."

O Goddess, if there be devotion, success is not far off for him. O fair-faced one, having abandoned the corruption of the syllables by the guru, his son, or the practitioner himself, one should reveal the mantra once again.
The practitioner, composed and together with the Guru or his son,
should restore the lost syllables and reveal the mantra once again;
likewise, by means of the division of the wheel, he should form a hexagon using the *yonimudrā*.
O fair-faced one, O Great Goddess, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times with a single utterance;
this cuts away the defects [incurred] from the Guru and others. Having performed one hundred thousand recitations himself, the Guru should cause the disciple to hear that mantra three times.
There is no doubt that this brings peace to the short and the long [vowels] as well as their defects;
O Daughter of the Mountain, O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times according to the path taught by the Guru, his son, or the practitioner himself.
Thereafter, one should perform oblations amounting to one-tenth of that, and then carry out the libations (tarpaṇa) and other rites.
Even after that, if the practitioner has not yet attained a steady mind,
then for the sake of the disciple's liberation, the rite must indeed be performed fourfold.
Even if death were to occur for him, he would still partake in liberation;
there is no doubt that the pacification of faults occurs through the recitation [of the mantra],
O Daughter of the Mountain, even when performed in a cremation ground or while speaking it in a dream.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times according to the stated path;
thereafter, one should perform the oblation (*homa*) ten times that amount, and then carry out the libation (*tarpaṇa*) and other rites.
Even after that, if the practitioner has not yet attained a steady mind, [he must continue].
Indeed, one should perform the previously mentioned worship fourfold;
one should undertake the first journey on a Tuesday or a Saturday.
One should worship the Goddess for seven days, or one should worship the player of the *turīya* drum.
I shall describe the practice of the cremation ground; listen with a one-pointed mind.
Having offered gold, silver, and likewise cloth, one should perform the preliminary consecration (varaṇa).
A golden seat, four finger-breadths in width, should be provided.
The honey-mixture (madhuparka) fit for enjoyment should be offered as prescribed; with whatever garment the queen is pleased, she should be gratified by that garment,
and one should provide appropriate ornaments in each respective place.
One should offer various kinds of delightful food-offerings (naivedya) consisting of diverse substances:
meat, rice, molasses, goat, wine, flour-cakes, and milk-porridge;
these articles of enjoyment should be placed in the water if the consumer is not present.
Having thus completed the preliminary worship, one should first perform the worship of Śiva. One should worship twenty-one liṅgas with the sixteen types of offerings,
and [offer] one hundred and eight bilva leaves smeared with sandalwood paste.
One should worship the mantra one thousand times for each [deity], Gajantaka included;
afterwards, O fair-faced one, one should perform a thousand oblations with bilva leaves.
When this is done, one obtains peace and long life; of this there is no doubt.
The Mātṛkābhedatantra, Chapter Thirteen.
The venerable Caṇḍikā said:
Listen, O Lord, Supreme Bliss, Sovereign of the worlds both supreme and subordinate!
Now I wish to hear: what kind of recitation is there for a rosary? What rosary belongs to which deity? Tell me that with a concentrated mind.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
One should wear a garland of *tulasī* for Vaiṣṇava rites, an elephant tusk for Gaṇeśvara,
and one should mutter the great mantra of Kālikā with a rosary of *rudrākṣa* beads.
The practitioner of mantra should recite the mantra of Tārā using a rosary known as the *mahāśaṅkha*;
with a rosary known as the *mahāśaṅkha*, the wise one should recite every vidyā.
Indeed, through a rosary known as the *mahāśaṅkha*, great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*) is attained spontaneously.
In the same way, all the sciences (vidyās) always reside within the great conch.
One should perform the recitation (japa) of the entire [mantra] using a crystal [bead] for all the gods, or with coral;
likewise, one may employ [beads] made of gold or silver for all the deities.

One should always perform the recitation for Kālikā and Sundarī with rudrākṣa beads; O Dear One, the practitioner of mantra should perform the recitation for Bhairavī with those known as śaṅkha and padma. In the ritual of Dhūmāvatī, one should perform the recitation with a garland made of dhustūra seeds in a cremation ground.
Thus, O beloved, I have explained to you the determination of the great rosary (mahāmālā).
Now, O beloved, listen with a concentrated mind as I shall describe the knots (granthi),
by means of which the rosary becomes perfectly accomplished and bestows all fruits upon men.
O Beloved,
in the fifty-one-bead rosary, O Supreme Goddess, there is one additional knot that bestows fruit; the rosary should be provided with a *brahmagranthi* and wound two and a half times.
O Goddess, it is a captivating serpent-noose with a foot-long binding;
O Supreme Sovereign, one should fashion it everywhere upon the garland of all the gods,
either by making a Brahma-knot in this manner or likewise as a serpent-noose.
O Goddess, one should cause an additional single knot to be made in the garland;
O Dear One, it should be strung together with the root mantra or with the *praṇava*.
And in the middle of the knots, one should fashion a most beautiful bead.
O Great Goddess, one should then cause the two threads to meet;
then one should perform the "Meru" and the "Stringing," with a knot joined above that.
Having thus fashioned the rosary, one should conceal it with great effort.
One should never manifest trembling, shaking, or noise therein;
likewise, [an arrow] falling from the hand or being cut off is a cause of great obstacles.
In the case of trembling, there is a loss of accomplishment; shaking brings much suffering.
If a sound occurs, disease will arise; if it falls from the hand, it causes destruction.
If the thread is severed, death will occur; therefore, one should be diligent.
Knowing this, O Maheśānī, one should perform rites for peace and well-being.
If one recites the mantra during the shaking [of the vessel] and it bestows success, then,
having diligently brought the guru, one should worship the chosen deity with twenty-two types of offerings after performing the installation of the ritual jar (kumbha).
Then, O beautiful one, he should offer one hundred and eight oblations with *bilva* leaves according to the rite of being smeared with the three sweets (*trimadhu*);
and likewise, O Caṇḍī, the wise practitioner should perform this even during the shaking and the chanting that is accompanied by sound.
Likewise, if [the rosary] falls from the hand or is broken, one should perform the *puraścaraṇa* rite;
at the conclusion of the recitation (*japa*) and other rites, one should worship the Goddess with the sixteen types of service (*upacāra*).
One should recite the mantra every day and offer the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) every day.
One should complete all rites according to the measure of the five limbs.
O Supreme Goddess, if one is poor or prone to obstacles,
one should perform a great worship at the beginning and the end and recite the mantra a thousand times.
Thereafter, one should offer a thousand oblations for the pacification of all obstacles;
having bathed [the deity] with the water from the pitcher, one should again cause the garland to be offered.
By this very procedure, one is not defiled by the nets of obstacles.
The Mātṛkābhedatantra,
the fourteenth chapter;
the venerable Caṇḍikā said:
By the mere retention of the mantra, at that very moment,
the individual soul (jīvātman) becomes one with it within the center of the Kuṇḍalinī, like the flame of a lamp. The Kuṇḍalinī, residing within the body, is the form of one’s own chosen deity.
"That very [power] residing in the body is enjoyed; what concern is there for the practitioner?
Tell me that, O Mahādeva, if I am dear to you.
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Goddess, enjoyment is threefold, according to the sequence of the divine, the hero, and the animal.

If Kuṇḍalī is enjoyed while remaining in the divine state and free from attachment— Kuṇḍalī who resides at the tip of the tongue for the hero, O you who are praised by heroes— then [enjoyment is divine].
And for the pleasure of the Great Goddess, the sacrificial animal is consumed as a favor;
the twice-born attains a divine state that always bestows liberation.
Such a Brahmin becomes a hero and one who has attained liberation—of this there is no doubt.
If even a beast endowed with devotion attains the grace [of the Lord], then the great liberation, such as *sāyujya* (union), is ordained for Kṣatriyas and others;
one certainly becomes an enjoyer of heaven, for there is no requirement of formal qualification at the time of death.
By the grace of Mahādevī, one attains another birth;
the vision of the Divine Hero (Divyavīra) arises—of this there is no doubt.
By the grace of the Divine Hero, one attains liberation (nirvāṇa)—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, he who enjoys [the fruits of] grace is a bound soul (paśu); of this there is no doubt.
For one who remains in the state of a bound soul, there is no eligibility for death;
indeed, liberation shall not come to him, and he will certainly undergo rebirth.
The illustrious Caṇḍikā said:
"Tell me, O Supreme Lord, the characteristics of the divine hero (divyavīra),
by the attainment of which the great liberation of the divine hero shall come to pass."
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
The goddess Vāruṇī is directly composed of Brahman;
though she was cursed, by the mere release from that curse, she became the supreme nectar in the form of Brahman.
Whatever is offered to the Great Goddess, that indeed becomes [hers];
one should visualize the Kuṇḍalinī from the Mūlādhāra up to the tip of the tongue.
By merely placing it in her mouth, the practitioner becomes possessed of knowledge.
Just as the goddess Kuṇḍalinī is situated within the center of the body,
so too should one meditate upon Vāruṇī as one's own chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) within the limbs of the *kalā*.
With a state of equanimity toward Kuṇḍalinī, one should cause [the offering] to be presented at the mouth of Śakti.
One should certainly accept the great purifier that is one's own leavings— the supreme nectar from his mouth— with a sense of identity, O fair-faced one.
Even the consideration of "leavings" and so forth never exists in Brahman.
"The water of the Gaṅgā is the Supreme Brahman; tell me, to whom does its grace belong?
Or to whom might the water of the ocean where the Gaṅgā meets it be a source of grace?
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain: merely by bathing in that water..."
Indeed, by bathing and immersing oneself, a mortal shall become a partaker of liberation;
for at the time of bathing, one immerses oneself from the feet up to the head.
O Daughter of the Mountain, contact with the feet causes no fault regarding the Supreme Brahman.
"And likewise, O Supreme Goddess, when [the self] has merged into the Supreme Self—
thus, O Goddess, have I told you the characteristics of the Divine Hero;
and the majesty has been told in the Vīra-tantra, O Beloved of Life."
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the characteristics of the *sādhikā* as well:
the divine power (*divyaśakti*), the hero’s power (*vīraśakti*), the teacher’s power (*guruśakti*), and likewise the supreme (*parā*),
the family power (*kulaśakti*), the passionate woman (*kāminī*), the ninefold power (*navaśakti*), and the young girl (*kumārikā*).
One should worship the Śrī-guru with devotion, even to the extent of offering one's own body;
otherwise, the suppression of one's own body will certainly occur.
For seven lifetimes, that goddess shall be a Pukkasi woman, deprived of a husband.
Considering one's own beloved to be Śiva, one should perform the means of worship;
O Supreme Goddess, one should never worship any other person.
O Caṇḍī, from worshipping another, total destruction will certainly occur.
The beloved will be deprived of longevity and face misfortune at every step;
there will be constant loss of wealth, and the wrath of the Goddess will arise.
Therefore, one must certainly and constantly worship the eternal Guru and the Divine.
She who engages in deliberations regarding what is auspicious or inauspicious in the presence of the Guru—her mantra shall be joined with wrath, and she shall meet with calamity at every step.
It is better to endure censure from the mouths of people; it is better to renounce one's life.
Nevertheless, one should worship the God who directly bestows liberation.
One should always avoid fear and deceit when performing the worship of the Guru.
If one maintains the splendor of the illustrious Guru through devotion, [one attains the goal].
Truth, truth, and again truth: Kāśī is that; there is no doubt in this.
O Supreme Goddess, if one should perform her retention (dhāraṇa), recitation (japa), worship (pūjā), and so forth without devotion, she would consume him with her splendor.
The illustrious Caṇḍikā said:
One should worship the Lord, the Guru who bestows liberation, together with his consort;
having abandoned attachment to him, how can one achieve self-discipline?
Śrī Śaṅkara said:
Listen, O Goddess; I shall speak according to the command of my guru.
One who is personally free from desire should maintain the fiery energy with devotion.
Since the wife of the guru and the son of the illustrious guru are both [his offspring],
the wife of the guru is the guru himself, and the son of the guru is undoubtedly the guru;
by worshipping one, O beloved, there is the worship of both.

Gaṇeśa is the son of the Guru, and Ṣaḍānana is also the son of the Guru. O beloved, she who is always devoted to worship should never worship one son of the Guru while neglecting the other son of the Guru.
One should never fail to worship either a hero or one of divine form;
O Goddess, by worshipping even one of them, one becomes a master of the great siddhis.
If a woman should perform the worship of both, she attains three or four [siddhis].
All her meditation, recitation, worship, and so forth, becomes entirely fruitless.
O Goddess, if by the power of fortune she should obtain even one son of a Guru—
one who is pleasing, a knower of the scriptures, and devoted to both restraint and grace— [then her efforts bear fruit].

One should perform worship— which bestows liberation— even at the cost of one's life, toward one who is handsome, intoxicated by youth, equal to a preceptor, and has conquered the senses; for if one does not worship such a person out of delusion, that very act becomes sinful.
